checks.title: SES identities are verified for sending and have DKIM enabled with SUCCESS status

verify.offenders: (VerifiedForSendingStatus != `true` || (IdentityType != 'EMAIL_ADDRESS' && (DkimAttributes.Status != 'SUCCESS' || DkimAttributes.SigningEnabled != `true`))) && [{detail: {identity_type: IdentityType, verified_for_sending: VerifiedForSendingStatus, dkim_status: DkimAttributes.Status, dkim_signing_enabled: DkimAttributes.SigningEnabled, dkim_origin: DkimAttributes.SigningAttributesOrigin}}] || `[]`
verify.pass_when_text: Neither Drata nor Vanta has an SES test: this is a check of the skill's own (the email evidence auditors ask for is at the DNS and configuration level). Every identity (domain or address) has VerifiedForSendingStatus=true. Domain identities also have DKIM signing enabled (SigningEnabled=true) with DkimAttributes.Status=SUCCESS, whether Easy DKIM (SigningAttributesOrigin=AWS_SES) or BYODKIM. Verified email addresses (EMAIL_ADDRESS) do not require their own DKIM: they are signed with the domain's DKIM. PENDING, FAILED, TEMPORARY_FAILURE and NOT_STARTED fail: the DKIM CNAME records are not published or do not resolve.

steps: Get the DKIM tokens of {resource_id} and publish, in the domain's DNS, one CNAME record per token (with Easy DKIM, 3 tokens).
Wait for DNS to propagate (it can take up to 72 hours) until Status changes to SUCCESS.
If signing is off, enable it with put-email-identity-dkim-attributes.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
# only if the identity uses BYODKIM or has no Easy DKIM: on an identity that already uses Easy DKIM it rotates the tokens and changes the CNAMEs
aws sesv2 put-email-identity-dkim-signing-attributes --email-identity "{resource_id}" --signing-attributes-origin AWS_SES --region "$REGION"
remediation.notes: No downtime. The first block moves the identity to Easy DKIM and returns the tokens (if it already uses Easy DKIM, it is not needed): rotating the tokens changes the CNAME records. For each token, publish in DNS (Route 53 console or the registrar) a CNAME TOKEN._domainkey.DOMAIN pointing to TOKEN.dkim.amazonses.com. Until the records resolve, the status stays PENDING. An unverified domain identity also needs the verification record shown in the SES console. Some registrars append the domain to the name on their own: in that case write only TOKEN._domainkey.

checks.title: The SES identity sends by default with a configuration set that requires TLS (TlsPolicy=REQUIRE)

verify.pass_when_text: Neither Drata nor Vanta has an SES test: this is a check of the skill's own (the email evidence auditors ask for is at the DNS and configuration level). Each identity has a default configuration set (get-email-identity, ConfigurationSetName) and that set has DeliveryOptions.TlsPolicy=REQUIRE: SES does not deliver to servers that do not negotiate TLS (the in-transit protection that CC6.7 looks for). Without a TlsPolicy the AWS default, OPTIONAL, applies, and it fails. An identity without a default configuration set fails, because SES only applies mandatory TLS through a set. The check evaluates the identity's default set: a set chosen on each send (for example with the X-SES-CONFIGURATION-SET header) is not evaluated. If the default set cannot be read with the auditor's permissions, that identity ends up NOT_VERIFIED.

steps: Choose or create a configuration set for {resource_id} and set its TlsPolicy to REQUIRE.
Leave that set as the identity's default configuration set.
Verify that the set has mandatory TLS and that the identity uses it by default.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
CONFIG_SET="__FILL_IN_CONFIGURATION_SET__"
aws sesv2 put-configuration-set-delivery-options --configuration-set-name "$CONFIG_SET" --tls-policy REQUIRE --region "$REGION"

REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
CONFIG_SET="__FILL_IN_CONFIGURATION_SET__"
aws sesv2 create-configuration-set --configuration-set-name "$CONFIG_SET" --delivery-options TlsPolicy=REQUIRE --region "$REGION" && aws sesv2 put-email-identity-configuration-set-attributes --email-identity "{resource_id}" --configuration-set-name "$CONFIG_SET" --region "$REGION"
remediation.notes: Risk: no downtime, but with TlsPolicy=REQUIRE SES does not deliver to recipients whose server does not support TLS (the message bounces): check the bounce metrics after the change. Use the first block if the identity already has a configuration set, and the second if it does not (it creates the set and makes it the default in a single step: the put only runs if the create succeeded). Replace __FILL_IN_CONFIGURATION_SET__ with the name of the set. Sends that specify another set on each message do not use the default set: configure those sets too.

checks.title: The identity's default configuration set has an enabled event destination

verify.pass_when_text: Neither Drata nor Vanta has an SES test: this is a check of the skill's own (the email evidence auditors ask for is at the DNS and configuration level). Each identity has a default configuration set with at least one enabled event destination (Enabled=true), for example SNS, CloudWatch or Firehose. Without an event destination nobody learns about bounces or complaints. An identity without a default configuration set fails. The check does not require specific event types; to operate email, at least BOUNCE and COMPLAINT are advisable. A set chosen on each send is not evaluated. If it cannot be read with the auditor's permissions, the identity ends up NOT_VERIFIED.

steps: Decide where the bounce and complaint events of {resource_id} go: a team SNS topic, CloudWatch or Firehose.
Create the event destination on the identity's default configuration set, with at least BOUNCE and COMPLAINT.
Verify the destination and subscribe a team mailbox to the topic.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
CONFIG_SET="__FILL_IN_CONFIGURATION_SET__"
TOPIC_ARN="__FILL_IN_SNS_TOPIC_ARN__"
aws sesv2 create-configuration-set-event-destination --configuration-set-name "$CONFIG_SET" --event-destination-name eventos-sns --event-destination '{"Enabled":true,"MatchingEventTypes":["BOUNCE","COMPLAINT"],"SnsDestination":{"TopicArn":"'"$TOPIC_ARN"'"}}' --region "$REGION"
remediation.notes: No downtime. Replace __FILL_IN_CONFIGURATION_SET__ with the identity's default configuration set (aws sesv2 get-email-identity shows the name; if it has none, see EML-002) and __FILL_IN_SNS_TOPIC_ARN__ with a topic in the same region. The topic needs a policy that lets ses.amazonaws.com publish; otherwise the events do not arrive. A set that already has an event destination with the same name fails on creation: choose another name. Add confirmed subscriptions to the topic so that someone receives the notices (see MON-007 for alarms).

checks.title: The sending domain has an SPF record (v=spf1)

verify.pass_when_text: Neither Drata nor Vanta has an SES test: this is a check of the skill's own (the email evidence auditors ask for is at the DNS and configuration level). Each SES domain identity (email addresses are not evaluated) has a TXT record on the domain itself that contains v=spf1. The engine queries public DNS with dig or nslookup. It does not verify that the record includes amazonses.com or the custom MAIL FROM: only that the domain publishes an SPF policy. If there are no domain identities, the result is N/A (empty); if DNS cannot be queried, NOT_VERIFIED.

steps: In the DNS of {resource_id} (Route 53 console or the registrar's panel), check whether a TXT record that starts with v=spf1 already exists.
If it does not exist, create a TXT record on {resource_id} with the value v=spf1 include:amazonses.com ~all.
If it already exists, add include:amazonses.com to it before the ~all or -all: a domain cannot have two SPF records.
Wait for DNS to propagate and verify with dig.
remediation.notes: No downtime. A domain with two SPF records fails SPF (PermError): edit the existing one, do not add another. If the domain uses a custom SES MAIL FROM, SPF aligns with that subdomain and the SPF record goes there (SES shows the MX and the TXT). Choosing ~all (softfail) or -all (hardfail) is a team policy decision. With the SPF limit of 10 DNS lookups, check the total if the domain already includes several services.

checks.title: The sending domain has DMARC with a quarantine or reject policy

verify.pass_when_text: Neither Drata nor Vanta has an SES test: this is a check of the skill's own (the email evidence auditors ask for is at the DNS and configuration level). Each SES domain identity (email addresses are not evaluated) has a TXT record at _dmarc.DOMAIN with a p=quarantine or p=reject policy. With no DMARC record, or with p=none (monitoring only), it fails with high severity: the domain can be spoofed. The engine queries public DNS with dig or nslookup. The pattern is anchored to the p= tag (case-insensitive): sp=reject or a p=none with sp=reject do not count. If there are no domain identities, the result is N/A (empty); if DNS cannot be queried, NOT_VERIFIED.

steps: Create a team mailbox that receives the DMARC aggregate reports (rua).

Publish in the DNS of {resource_id} (Route 53 console or the registrar's panel) a TXT record at _dmarc.{resource_id} with the value v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:__FILL_IN_DMARC_EMAIL__ to start observing. If the domain already has a _dmarc record, edit it instead of creating another (there can be only one): if it already says p=none, keep it and continue with the reports.
Review the reports for a few weeks and fix the legitimate sources that fail SPF or DKIM.
Raise the policy to p=quarantine and, when there are no false positives, to p=reject. The check only passes with quarantine or reject.
Wait for DNS to propagate and verify with dig.
remediation.notes: No downtime, but p=quarantine and p=reject make receivers send to spam or reject mail that fails DMARC: start with p=none and raise gradually, or legitimate mail (invoices, notices) is lost. DMARC passes if SPF or DKIM pass and are aligned with the From domain. SES aligns DKIM with the identity's domain when Easy DKIM is used (see EML-001). Replace __FILL_IN_DMARC_EMAIL__ with a team mailbox. Subdomains inherit the organizational domain's policy unless sp= is defined or they have their own _dmarc record (RFC 7489): if the sending subdomain has no _dmarc of its own, check the parent domain's record before acting.

checks.title: The region's SES account has production access and an account-level suppression list

verify.pass_when_text: Neither Drata nor Vanta has an SES test: this is a check of the skill's own (the email evidence auditors ask for is at the DNS and configuration level). In each region that has SES identities, get-account returns ProductionAccessEnabled=true and SuppressionAttributes.SuppressedReasons with at least one reason (BOUNCE or COMPLAINT). An account in the sandbox only sends to verified addresses and with a low quota; without a suppression list, sends are repeated to addresses that bounce and reputation is damaged. One row is reported per identity in the region, because the problem belongs to the SES account. A region without identities is not evaluated.

steps: In the SES console of region {region}, go to Account dashboard and choose Request production access (it is an AWS support case: describe the use case, how bounces and complaints are handled, and how recipients are obtained).
In Suppression list, open Account-level settings and enable suppression for Bounces and Complaints.
Verify with get-account that ProductionAccessEnabled is true and that SuppressedReasons has the reasons.
remediation.notes: Leaving the sandbox cannot be requested with the AWS CLI: it is a support case that AWS approves (it usually takes up to a day). The account-level suppression list can be changed with aws sesv2 put-account-suppression-attributes --suppressed-reasons BOUNCE COMPLAINT, but the blocking part is production access. An SES account that only sends to its own verified addresses may stay in the sandbox on purpose: document it and accept this finding.
